gui.ffmpeg_dialog_title: Select ffmpeg folder (folder containing ffmpeg.exe / ffmpeg)
gui.opt_dts_eac3_tip: Convert DTS audio tracks to E-AC3 640k during the remux. ffmpeg can only store DTS in MP4 as mp4a/esds – TVs then fail to recognize the file and refuse it entirely, even if they do support DTS. All other audio tracks are still copied unchanged, and so is the video.
gui.opt_local_copy_tip: Moves the movie to the local disk (default: Windows temp folder) before processing, works on it there completely, and transfers only the finished MP4 back to the NAS. This offloads the network and is significantly faster than working directly on the NAS. If an error occurs, the original MKV is automatically moved back to its NAS origin.

konvgui.title: Video converter
konvgui.subtitle: folder → MP4 (AMD accelerated)
konvgui.folder_hint: Shared with the main window – all video files in it are scanned; everything except .mp4 and .mkv is converted (resolution is preserved).
konvgui.opt_amd_tip: Uses the AMD AMF encoder of the graphics card (h264_amf / hevc_amf). It is verified with a short test at start; if it does not work, the software encoder is used automatically.
konvgui.opt_sar_tip: Old MPEG/DVD/WMV sources often have non-square pixels (SAR ≠ 1:1). With this option enabled the picture is rescaled to square pixels – otherwise the TV shows it distorted.
konvgui.opt_local_tip: Same as the remux part: the original is first moved to the local working folder, converted there, and only the finished MP4 is moved back to the source folder. This offloads the NAS. On any error the original is automatically moved back to its source location.
konvgui.err_workdir_missing: Working folder for local processing not set.
konvgui.opt_recursive_tip: Also searches all subfolders of the selected folder.
konvgui.opt_keep_tip: ON: after a successful conversion the original is backed up – into the main window's backup folder if that is set to "global", otherwise into an "old video" subfolder. OFF: the original is deleted.

konvgui.info_title: What does the video converter do?
konvgui.info_2: The main window remuxes Dolby Vision MKVs to MP4 losslessly. Everything
konvgui.info_3: that is NOT Dolby Vision and comes in an older format – AVI, WMV, MPG,
konvgui.info_4: MOV, FLV, VOB and the like – often cannot be played by the TV at all.
konvgui.info_5: The converter re-encodes those files into an MP4 an LG TV plays via direct
konvgui.info_6: play. MKV files are deliberately left alone; they belong to the remux part.
konvgui.info_9: 1. Scan: the selected folder (optionally including subfolders) is walked.
konvgui.info_10: Every file is analyzed with ffprobe – resolution, pixel aspect ratio,
konvgui.info_11: frame rate, field order, audio and subtitle tracks. The result is
konvgui.info_12: printed to the log as an overview.
konvgui.info_13: 2. Convert: every non-MP4 file is re-encoded. Existing MP4 targets and
konvgui.info_14: unknown file types are skipped and logged.
konvgui.info_17: You can choose H.264 or H.265 (HEVC). The default is H.265: about a third
konvgui.info_18: smaller at the same picture quality. H.264 is the safe choice for older
konvgui.info_20: Both run on the AMD hardware encoder (hevc_amf / h264_amf). Whether the
konvgui.info_21: card really supports it is verified at start with a real one-second test
konvgui.info_22: encode – the list in "ffmpeg -encoders" only proves the support was
konvgui.info_23: compiled in, not that it works. If the hardware refuses a particular file,
konvgui.info_24: the converter falls back to libx265 / libx264 for that file alone.
konvgui.info_27: Rate control uses a target bitrate (peak VBR) rather than a constant
konvgui.info_28: quantizer. Reason: with a constant quantizer, noisy old sources easily end
konvgui.info_29: up larger than the original. The bitrate scales with resolution and frame
konvgui.info_30: rate; the quality step (high / medium / small) shifts it up or down.
konvgui.info_32: # What is changed about the picture
konvgui.info_33: - Interlaced sources are deinterlaced (yadif) – the AMD hardware encoder
konvgui.info_35: - Anamorphic material (SAR other than 1:1, typical for DVD/MPEG/WMV) is
konvgui.info_36: rescaled to square pixels, otherwise the picture looks squashed.
konvgui.info_37: - The resolution is otherwise left untouched – nothing is upscaled.
konvgui.info_38: - Output: yuv420p, AAC audio (copied when the source is already AAC),
konvgui.info_39: a keyframe every 2 seconds for seeking, +faststart for instant start.
konvgui.info_42: With "process locally" enabled (the default) the original is moved to the
konvgui.info_43: work folder first, converted there, and only the finished MP4 is written
konvgui.info_44: back. That takes a lot of load off a NAS. If anything fails – encode,
konvgui.info_45: transfer back, stop button – the original is moved back to where it came
konvgui.info_47: With "create backup" enabled the original goes into the backup folder,
konvgui.info_48: otherwise it is deleted after a successful conversion.
konvgui.info_51: Simulation mode scans and logs everything but writes no file at all. Handy
konvgui.info_52: to see up front what a real run would do.
